sensesIntro.cn: 五种用法：同一事物自身施动、强调本身、独自行动、本质上如何，以及恢复常态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mirror standing before an object, identical inside and out.
core.cn: 核心意象：镜子立在物体前，镜内镜外一样。

branches.en: THE DOOR: the wind pushes it into itself.
branches.cn: 门这条线：风把它推回自己身上。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: old walls, new rooms.
branches.cn: 建筑这条线：旧墙与新房间。

branches.en: THE CHILD: buttons done without help.
branches.cn: 孩子这条线：不用人帮就扣上的扣子。

branches.en: THE OFFER: fair alone, wrong in timing.
branches.cn: 提议这条线：单看公道，时机不对。

branches.en: THE MARKET: shaken, then levelled again.
branches.cn: 市场这条线：震惊之后又回到原位。

intro.en: Itself joins two old English pieces, the pronoun it and the word self.
intro.cn: itself 把两块老英语成分拼在一起：代词 it 与 self。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; the nearest Latin pattern is the reflexive suus, listed only for contrast.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁语来源，最接近的拉丁模式是反身词 suus，只作对照。

items.example: The possessive built on the same stem.
Kept as one word, never split.
items.exampleCN: 始终写成一个词，不拆开。

definition_zh: 夹克；短外套；（书）护封；（管道、锅炉的）外壳
definition_en: a short coat with sleeves, or an outer cover around a book, machine, or pipe
core_image: 一件短外套搭在椅背上，袖口还留着上一位主人的形状
scene: 秋天的早晨有点凉，他把一件短外套从衣架上取下来披上。He grabbed a light jacket before leaving the house.
sceneCN: 这里 jacket 是「夹克」（第 1 个义项：有袖的短外套），句意为出门前他抓起一件薄夹克。画面里的物件：衣架、短外套、清晨的凉意。

pos.zh: 名词：夹克；短外套；护封；外壳
动词：给……加护封；给……加外壳

derivatives.zh: 由 jacket 加 -ed 构成，义为「穿外套的；有外壳的」
由 jacket 加 -ing 构成，义为「外套材料；护套」
由 jacket 加 -less 构成，义为「没穿外套的」

senses.title: A short coat
senses.definition: a short coat with sleeves that reaches only to the hips or waist
senses.definitionCN: 有袖子、只到臀部或腰部的短外套
senses.example: He wore a denim jacket to the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿了件牛仔夹克去听演唱会。
senses.why: The clothing sense is the earliest recorded use in French, naming a short tunic.
senses.whyCN: 衣物义是法语里最早有记录的用法，指一种短上衣。

senses.title: A protective cover
senses.definition: an outer casing fitted around a machine part, pipe, or tank to protect or cool it
senses.definitionCN: 包在机械零件、管道或贮罐外起保护或冷却作用的外层
senses.example: The boiler jacket keeps the heat inside.
senses.exampleCN: 锅炉外壳把热量留在里面。
senses.why: A jacket on a machine is a coat put on an object, so the clothing image transfers directly.
senses.whyCN: 机器上的 jacket 就是给物件穿的外套，衣物的画面直接搬了过去。

senses.title: A book's paper cover
senses.definition: the loose paper cover wrapped around a hardback book
senses.definitionCN: 包在精装书外面的那层可拆纸质封面
senses.example: The dust jacket is torn at the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 护封的角上撕破了。
senses.why: The paper cover dresses the book the way a jacket dresses a body.
senses.whyCN: 纸封面给书穿衣，就像夹克给人穿衣。

senses.title: An outer skin of a cable
senses.definition: the insulating layer around electrical wires or a cable
senses.definitionCN: 包在电线或电缆外面的绝缘层
senses.example: The cable jacket was cut, so the wire was replaced.
senses.exampleCN: 电缆护套破了，于是换掉了那根线。
senses.why: Insulation is another protective coat, keeping danger inside the cable.
senses.whyCN: 绝缘层又是一层保护衣，把危险留在电缆里。

senses.title: To cover with a jacket
senses.definition: to fit or cover something with a jacket or an outer layer
senses.definitionCN: 给某物装外套或加上外层
senses.example: Workers jacketed the pipes before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 入冬前工人给管道加上了外壳。
senses.why: The verb simply puts the coat on, the literal action behind the noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是把外套穿上，是名词背后的字面动作。

intro.en: Jacket came from Old French jaquette, a small jaque, which named a short tunic or coat of mail.
intro.cn: jacket 来自古法语 jaquette，是 jaque 的指小形式，指短的束腰衣或锁子甲衣。

items.en: jaque named a short tunic worn by soldiers.
items.cn: jaque 指士兵穿的短上衣。

items.en: -ette is a diminutive ending, so jaquette was a little jaque.
items.cn: 古法语 -ette 是指小词尾，jaquette 即小的 jaque。

items.en: Medieval records give jacottus or jacquetus for a short coat.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁文献写作 jacottus 或 jacquetus，指短外衣。

items.en: English borrowed jacket for a short coat, often of leather or mail.
items.cn: 英语借入 jacket，指短外衣，常为皮制或甲制。

items.en: The word spread to book covers, pipes, and machine casings.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到书封、管道与机器外壳。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the jack- shape; the near-meaning group holds outer garments and covers.
note.cn: 形近组是 jack- 开头的词形；近义组收外衣与外壳类词。

entries.definition: Wearing a jacket, or fitted with a casing.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「穿着外套的；有外壳的」。

entries.definition: Material used to cover pipes.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「护套材料」，同族名词。

entries.definition: Without a jacket.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -less 构成，义为「没穿外套的」。

entries.definition: A longer outer garment with sleeves.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「外套」，通常比 jacket 长。

entries.definition: A knitted jumper that opens at the front.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「开衫」，针织面料，前开扣。

entries.definition: Something that lies over or around a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「覆盖物」，最宽泛的外壳类词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the small tunic jaquette into pipes, books, and cables.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子跟着小小的 jaquette 走到管道、书本与电缆上。

normal.en: Old French jaque was a short soldier's tunic.
normal.cn: 古法语 jaque 是士兵的短上衣。

normal.en: The ending -ette makes it a small one.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ette 表示「小」。

normal.en: A dust jacket wraps a book like a coat.
normal.cn: dust jacket 像外套一样包住书。

normal.en: A life jacket is a jacket that keeps you up.
normal.cn: life jacket 是能让人浮起来的外套。

normal.en: A water jacket cools an engine with water.
normal.cn: water jacket 用水给发动机降温。

abstract.en: A jacket is the layer that goes over everything else.
abstract.cn: 夹克是穿在所有衣服外面的那一层。

abstract.en: A book put on a jacket is ready to be sold.
abstract.cn: 穿上护封的书才准备上市。

abstract.en: Every pipe needs a coat of its own.
abstract.cn: 每根管子都需要一件自己的外套。

examples.en: She zipped up her jacket against the wind.
examples.cn: 她拉上夹克拉链挡风。

examples.en: The book's jacket shows a photograph of the author.
examples.cn: 书的护封上印着作者的照片。

examples.en: The engine is enclosed in a water jacket.
examples.cn: 发动机被一个水套包住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「夹克特」—— 特意夹在身上的短外套

root: 古法语 jaque「士兵的短上衣」+ -ette（指小词尾）→ jaquette → 中古拉丁 jacottus → 中古英语 jacket。同族有 jacketed、jacketing。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: a short coat, a machine casing, a book's paper cover, a cable sheath, and the verb of covering.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：短外套、机器外壳、书护封、电缆护套，以及加外壳的动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a short coat hanging on a chair, still holding its shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：搭在椅背的短外套，还保持着原来的形状。

branches.en: THE CONCERT: denim over a thin shirt.
branches.cn: 演唱会这条线：薄衬衫外的牛仔布。

branches.en: THE BOILER: a casing that keeps heat in.
branches.cn: 锅炉这条线：留住热量的外壳。

branches.en: THE BOOK: loose paper over a hard cover.
branches.cn: 书本这条线：包住硬封的活页纸。

branches.en: THE CABLE: insulation cut down to the wire.
branches.cn: 电缆这条线：被切到铁芯的绝缘层。

branches.en: THE PIPES: workers wrapping them before winter.
branches.cn: 管道这条线：入冬前工人给它们包上外层。

intro.en: Jacket is a French borrowing; English adds only the familiar endings after it.
intro.cn: jacket 是从法语借来的，后面的英语词尾都是后来添上的。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin took the French word as jacottus, and its relatives are few.
latinIntro.cn: 中古拉丁语把这个法语词写成 jacottus，其同族词不多。

items.exampleCN: 英语写作 jacket，而非 jaquette。

items.example: A jacket for a printed book.

definition_zh: 牛仔裤；粗斜纹棉布裤
definition_en: trousers made of strong cotton cloth, usually blue, worn informally by people of any age
core_image: 两条磨得发白的厚棉布裤腿，口袋上钉着黄铜铆钉
scene: 衣柜最下面压着一条穿旧的裤子，膝盖处已经泛白。He pulled on his old jeans and went out to the corner store.
sceneCN: 这里 jeans 是「牛仔裤」（第 1 个义项：粗斜纹棉布做的裤子），句意为他套上旧牛仔裤就去街角小店了。画面里的物件：衣柜、泛白的膝部、门口。

pos.zh: 名词：牛仔裤；粗斜纹布裤（只用复数）

derivatives.zh: 由 jeans 去掉词尾 -s 而来，指牛仔布或牛仔裤单条
同类词，指牛仔布本身，法国布料名 Nîmes 缩合而成
由 jeans 加 -ed 构成，义为「穿着牛仔裤的」，多用于书面描写

senses.title: Trousers of strong cotton cloth
senses.definition: trousers made of a heavy twilled cotton fabric, usually dyed blue
senses.definitionCN: 用厚重的斜纹棉布做成的裤子，通常染成蓝色
senses.example: She bought a pair of jeans with a straight leg.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一条直筒牛仔裤。
senses.why: The word names the cloth before it names the trousers, and the trousers kept the plural shape of the cloth word.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指布料再指裤子，而裤子沿用了布料词的复数外形。

senses.title: A blue-cotton everyday uniform
senses.definition: such trousers worn as tough working clothes rather than as fashion
senses.definitionCN: 指作为耐磨工作服而非时装穿用的这种裤子
senses.example: Miners once wore jeans because the cloth refused to tear.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工当年穿牛仔裤，是因为这种布不容易撕破。
senses.why: The plural word carried the work-clothes sense long before fashion adopted it.
senses.whyCN: 在时装接手之前，这个复数词很久以来一直指工装。

senses.title: A fashion item with a cut or wash
senses.definition: a pair of such trousers treated as a styled garment, described by cut, wash, or finish
senses.definitionCN: 按剪裁、水洗或做旧处理来描述的时装裤装
senses.example: His ripped jeans cost more than my winter coat.
senses.exampleCN: 他那条破洞牛仔裤比我冬天的大衣还贵。
senses.why: Once the garment became a style object, the word picked up the whole vocabulary of cuts and washes.
senses.whyCN: 这条裤子成了时尚对象之后，这个词就带上了整套剪裁与水洗的说法。

senses.title: Denim cloth itself
senses.definition: the twilled cotton fabric from which such trousers are made
senses.definitionCN: 用来做这种裤子的斜纹棉布
senses.example: The jacket is made of dark jeans cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 这件夹克是用深色牛仔布做的。
senses.why: The fabric sense is the older layer of meaning and still survives in compounds.
senses.whyCN: 布料义是这个词更早的一层意思，至今还活在一些复合词里。

senses.title: A casual dress code
senses.definition: an informal standard of dress in which such trousers are acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 允许穿这类裤子的非正式着装标准
senses.example: The office allows jeans on Fridays.
senses.exampleCN: 公司允许周五穿牛仔裤上班。
senses.why: From a garment, the word grew into a label for a whole dress code.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从一件衣服长成了整套着装标准的标签。

intro.en: Jeans is a plural garment word that came into English from the name of a cloth, and the cloth name came from a city.
intro.cn: jeans 是一个复数形式的衣物词，先经由布料名进入英语，而布料名又来自一座城市的名字。

items.en: The cloth name Gene was used in French for a twilled cotton fabric made at Genoa.
items.cn: 法语用 Gene 指热那亚出产的斜纹棉布。

items.en: English borrowed the cloth word as jean or jene in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪把布料词借作 jean 或 jene。

items.en: The plural jeans first named such cloth and later the trousers cut from it.
items.cn: 复数形式 jeans 先指这种布，后来指用它裁成的裤子。

items.en: American workwear of the nineteenth century fixed the blue trousers sense.
items.cn: 十九世纪的美国工装固定了「蓝色长裤」这一义项。

items.en: Denim entered English by another route, from serge de Nîmes.
items.cn: denim 经由另一条路径进入英语，来自「尼姆的哔叽」这一布料名。

note.en: The look-alike group holds cloth and garment words that travel with jeans; the near-meaning group holds other everyday trousers.
note.cn: 形近组收与 jeans 同行的布料和衣物词；近义组收其他日常裤装词。

entries.definition: Heavy twilled cotton used for jeans.
entries.definitionCN: 指做牛仔裤的厚斜纹棉布，与 jeans 常成对出现，但拼写与来源都不同。

entries.definition: The singular form, naming the cloth or one pair.
entries.definitionCN: jeans 的单数形式，指牛仔布或一条裤子。

entries.definition: A general British word for a two-legged garment.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指裤子的英式说法，语法上同样常用复数。

entries.definition: The usual American word for trousers.
entries.definitionCN: 美式英语里最常见的「裤子」。

entries.definition: Smart casual trousers, not denim.
entries.definitionCN: 指较正式的休闲长裤，一般不用牛仔布。

entries.definition: Light cotton trousers in plain colours.
entries.definitionCN: 指素色薄棉布休闲裤。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the city of Genoa to the Friday dress code.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从热那亚这座城走到周五的休闲着装。

normal.en: The cloth name came from Genoa, Italian Genova.
normal.cn: 布料名来自热那亚，意大利语作 Genova。

normal.en: Jeans is normally plural, like trousers and glasses.
normal.cn: jeans 通常用复数，和 trousers、glasses 一样。

normal.en: A pair of jeans is the standard counting pattern.
normal.cn: 计数的标准说法是 a pair of jeans。

normal.en: Denim and jeans are near twins but took different routes.
normal.cn: denim 与 jeans 像双胞胎，但来路不同。

normal.en: Blue jeans fixed the colour sense in American workwear.
normal.cn: 蓝色牛仔裤在美国工装里固定了这个颜色义。

abstract.en: A pair of jeans is a city folded into a pocket.
abstract.cn: 一条牛仔裤就是一座城市折进了口袋。

abstract.en: The rivets are little guarantees that the cloth will hold.
abstract.cn: 铆钉是布料不裂开的小小保证。

abstract.en: Faded knees are a calendar written in cloth.
abstract.cn: 磨白的膝盖是写在布上的日历。

examples.en: These jeans are too tight around the waist.
examples.cn: 这条牛仔裤腰部太紧了。

examples.en: He wears jeans to work on casual days.
examples.cn: 轻松的上班日他穿牛仔裤。

examples.en: The shop sells jeans in every shade of blue.
examples.cn: 这家店卖各种深浅的蓝色牛仔裤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「紧死」—— 牛仔裤穿太紧，就真的紧死了

root: 来自法语布料名 Gene，源于意大利城市 Genoa（热那亚）；十六世纪进入英语作 jean，复数 jeans 后指用它缝制的长裤。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: the cotton trousers, their use as work clothes, their life as fashion, the cloth itself, and the dress code they stand for.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：棉布长裤本身、作为工装、作为时装、布料本身，以及它所代表的休闲着装。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thick blue cotton cut into two legs and held by rivets.
core.cn: 核心意象：厚蓝棉布裁成两条裤腿，用铆钉钉牢。

branches.en: THE CLOTH LINE: a fabric that became a pair of trousers.
branches.cn: 布料这条线：一种布变成了裤子。

branches.en: THE MINE LINE: work clothes that refuse to tear.
branches.cn: 矿井这条线：撕不破的工装。

branches.en: THE SHOP WINDOW: cuts, washes, and rips sold as style.
branches.cn: 橱窗这条线：剪裁、水洗、破洞都能卖。

branches.en: THE OFFICE LINE: a garment that marks a whole relaxed day.
branches.cn: 办公室这条线：一件衣服标出整个轻松的日子。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY LINE: tough cloth that also looks personal.
branches.cn: 日常这条线：耐磨的布也能显得有个性。

intro.en: Jeans is borrowed whole, so English adds only endings; the visible endings are the plural -s and the adjective -ed.
intro.cn: jeans 是整体借来的词，英语只添词尾；看得见的是复数 -s 与形容词 -ed。

latinIntro.en: The word comes from a place name rather than a Latin root, so the Latin relatives below are city-name forms only.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词来自地名而非拉丁词根，下面的拉丁条目只是城市名的形式。

items.example: The weaver sold jean by the metre.
The cloth was shipped from Genoa.
It feels like a denimy blue.

items.exampleCN: 蓝色牛仔裤是最常见的。

definition_zh: 工作；职业；任务；活儿；职位
definition_en: the paid work that someone does regularly, or one particular task that has to be done
core_image: 一张排满格子的日程表，每格都写着待办的事
scene: 面试结束后，她站在走廊里等电梯，手里还捏着简历。She spent three months looking for a job in the city.
sceneCN: 这里 job 是「工作、职业」（第 1 个义项：为取得报酬而长期做的事），句意为她在这座城市找工作找了三个月。画面里的物件：走廊、电梯、简历。

pos.zh: 名词：工作；职业；职位；任务；活儿
动词：打零工（口语）

derivatives.zh: 由 job 加 -less 构成，义为「失业的」
由 job 加 -ing 构成，义为「打零工的；做零活的」
由 job 加 -er 构成，指散户经纪或做零活的人

senses.title: Paid work done regularly
senses.definition: the regular paid work that a person does to earn a living
senses.definitionCN: 一个人为谋生而长期从事的有偿工作
senses.example: She found a job in a bookshop near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她在车站附近的书店找到了一份工作。
senses.why: The core sense is regular paid work, the thing a person most often asks another about.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是长期有偿工作，也就是人们最常问起的那件事。

senses.title: A position in a firm
senses.definition: a particular post or opening that someone can be hired to fill
senses.definitionCN: 某个可以被雇用填补的具体岗位
senses.example: Fifty people applied for the job.
senses.exampleCN: 有五十人申请这个岗位。
senses.why: A job can be seen as a slot to be filled, separate from the person filling it.
senses.whyCN: job 也能被看作一个待填的位置，与填它的人分开。

senses.title: A single task
senses.definition: one particular piece of work that must be finished
senses.definitionCN: 一件必须完成的特定工作
senses.example: Cleaning the gutters is a nasty job.
senses.exampleCN: 清理屋檐水槽是件麻烦的任务。
senses.why: The countable task sense narrows regular work down to one piece of it.
senses.whyCN: 可数的任务义把长期工作缩成其中的一件。

senses.title: Quality of work done
senses.definition: the standard or quality of a piece of work, as in doing a good job
senses.definitionCN: 某项工作的水准，如「干得好」
senses.example: You did a good job on that report.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告你写得不错。
senses.why: Judging how a job was done blends the task sense with an evaluation.
senses.whyCN: 评价活儿干得怎么样，是任务义与评价的融合。

senses.title: A fixed duty or role
senses.definition: something treated as a duty that belongs to a person
senses.definitionCN: 被视为某人分内应做的事
senses.example: It is not my job to answer the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 接电话不是我的职责。
senses.why: When a duty is assigned, the word slides from the work to the person expected to do it.
senses.whyCN: 当职责被指派时，这个词就从工作滑到了该做工作的人身上。

senses.title: To work by the piece
senses.definition: to do small or piece-rate work, often casually
senses.definitionCN: 做零散或计件的工作，多为临时性质
senses.example: He jobbed on building sites for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 他在工地打了一年零工。
senses.why: The verb keeps only the piecework shadow of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词只保留了名词「零活」的那道影子。

intro.en: Job is a word of uncertain origin; the usual view links it to a lump or piece of work, but the earlier steps are disputed.
intro.cn: job 的来源一般认为不确定；常见看法把它连到「一块、一桩」的活儿，但更早的脉络尚有争议。

items.en: The word appears in English in the sixteenth century with the sense of a piece of work.
items.cn: 这个词十六世纪出现于英语，义为「一桩活儿」。

items.en: Some scholars connect it with gob, a lump or mass, meaning a lump of work.
items.cn: 一些学者把它连到 gob「一块、一团」，意为一团活儿。

items.en: Others treat it as unrelated slang of unknown source.
items.cn: 另一些人认为它是来源不明的俚语，与此无关。

items.en: By the seventeenth century it meant regular paid employment.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，它已指长期的有偿雇用。

items.en: The verb and the phrases do a good job spread in the modern period.
items.cn: 动词用法与 do a good job 一类说法在近现代铺开。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words that are easy to confuse with job; the near-meaning group holds other words for work and tasks.
note.cn: 形近组收容易与 job 混看的短词；近义组收表示工作与任务的其他词。

entries.definition: To run slowly and steadily.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写只差一个字母，义为「慢跑」，来源不同。

entries.definition: To write something down quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近，义为「匆匆记下」，来源不同。

entries.definition: A shrub grown for its oil.
entries.definitionCN: 拼写相近的植物名，来源完全不同。

entries.definition: Activity done to achieve a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 不可数的「工作」，范围比 job 宽。

entries.definition: The whole course of a working life.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个职业生涯，比 job 长。

entries.definition: One piece of work to be done.
entries.definitionCN: 指一项具体任务，与第 3 个义项最近。

entries.definition: A particular position of employment.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式的「职位」，与第 2 个义项相近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a lump of work to a slot in the job market.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从「一团活儿」走到就业市场里的一个空位。

normal.en: Job is countable, so we say a job and two jobs.
normal.cn: job 可数，说 a job、two jobs。

normal.en: Work is usually uncountable, which is the classic contrast.
normal.cn: work 通常不可数，这是最经典的对比。

normal.en: A job interview is where a person meets a post.
normal.cn: job interview 是人去会一个岗位的场合。

normal.en: Do a good job judges the task, not the post.
normal.cn: do a good job 评的是活儿，不是岗位。

normal.en: Jobless adds -less to turn the noun into an adjective.
normal.cn: jobless 加 -less 把名词变成形容词。

abstract.en: A job is a box on a timetable that someone pays to fill.
abstract.cn: 工作是日程表上有人付钱让人填的一格。

abstract.en: The same word covers a life and an afternoon.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指一辈子也指一个下午。

abstract.en: Every task is a small job inside a big one.
abstract.cn: 每项任务都是大活儿里的小活儿。

examples.en: He took a job at a small factory.
examples.cn: 他在一家小厂找了份工作。

examples.en: Finishing the roof was a two-day job.
examples.cn: 修完屋顶是两天的活儿。

examples.en: She did a fine job of explaining the rules.
examples.cn: 她把规则解释得很清楚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「找不着」—— 没活儿干的人，天天在找 job

root: 来源一般认为不确定；常见假说与 gob「一块、一团」相关，即「一团活儿」，另一说认为是来源不明的俚语。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: regular paid work, a post, one task, the quality of work, a fixed duty, and the verb for piecework.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：长期有偿工作、岗位、单项任务、活儿的质量、分内职责，以及打零工的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a filled square on a timetable, each square paid for.
core.cn: 核心意象：日程表上一格一格被填满、并且有人付钱的方块。

branches.en: THE DESK LINE: work that repeats every weekday.
branches.cn: 办公桌这条线：每个工作日重复的工作。

branches.en: THE NOTICE BOARD: an opening that many people want.
branches.cn: 公告栏这条线：许多人争的一个空位。

branches.en: THE CHORE LINE: one task and how well it was done.
branches.cn: 杂活这条线：一项任务以及干得好不好。

branches.en: THE ROTA: the duty that belongs to a name.
branches.cn: 值班表这条线：写着一个名字的职责。

branches.en: THE SITE LINE: casual work paid by the piece.
branches.cn: 工地这条线：按件付钱的零活。

intro.en: Job is a short native-style word; English builds its family with endings rather than a Latin stem.
intro.cn: job 是很短的英语词，词族靠英语词尾扩展，没有拉丁词干。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root behind job, so the list below stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: job 背后没有拉丁词根，因此下面留空。

items.example: He does odd jobs for neighbours.

definition_zh: 加入；连接；参加；把……接起来；会合
definition_en: to become a member of a group, or to fasten two or more things together so that they touch or form one thing
core_image: 两块木料被一道榫头咬合在一起，接缝看不出来
scene: 社团招新的长桌摆在广场中央，路过的人停下填表。Over a hundred students joined the club in its first week.
sceneCN: 这里 join 是「加入」（第 1 个义项：成为某个团体的成员），句意为社团成立第一周就有一百多名学生加入。画面里的物件：长桌、表格、广场。

pos.zh: 动词：加入；参加；连接；会合

derivatives.zh: 由 join 加 -t 构成，指接合处或关节
由 joint 加 -ly 构成，义为「共同地、连带地」
由 join 加 -er 构成，义为「细木工匠」
由 join 加 -ing 构成，义为「连接；接合处」
加 en- 前缀构成，义为「责令；禁止」

senses.title: To become a member
senses.definition: to become a member of a group, club, company, or organization
senses.definitionCN: 成为某个团体、社团、公司或组织的成员
senses.example: She joined the debating society in her first term.
senses.exampleCN: 她在第一个学期加入了辩论社。
senses.why: Membership is a joining of oneself to a body, the same act as joining two things.
senses.whyCN: 加入就是把自己接到一个群体上，与把两样东西接起来是同一个动作。

senses.title: To fasten things together
senses.definition: to fasten two or more things so that they are linked or become one
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或多个东西接在一起，使其相连或成为一体
senses.example: Join the two pipes with a short metal collar.
senses.exampleCN: 用一段短金属箍把两根管子接起来。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical layer: two edges brought to touch.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的物理层含义：两条边被凑到一起。

senses.title: To take part in an activity
senses.definition: to take part in something that others are already doing
senses.definitionCN: 参与别人已经在做的事
senses.example: Do come and join the game after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后一定来参加游戏。
senses.why: Taking part is joining one activity rather than one organization.
senses.whyCN: 参加指的是加入一项活动，而不是一个组织。

senses.title: To meet and merge
senses.definition: to meet and combine, as roads, rivers, or people on a route
senses.definitionCN: 指道路、河流或路上的人在一点汇合
senses.example: The two paths join just below the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 两条小路就在桥下会合。
senses.why: Two lines meeting is the physical joining seen from the path itself.
senses.whyCN: 两条线交汇，就是站在路的角度看的「接合」。

senses.title: To share in a feeling or action
senses.definition: to share an action or feeling with someone, often in a set phrase
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法中与他人共同做某事或共有某种感受
senses.example: The whole hall joined in the chorus.
senses.exampleCN: 全场一起唱起了副歌。
senses.why: Joining a voice to others extends the fastener image to sound and feeling.
senses.whyCN: 把自己的声音接到别人那里，是把接合的画面延伸到声音与情绪上。

intro.en: Join comes from French joindre, from Latin jungere, "to yoke or connect"; the same root gives junction and jugular.
intro.cn: join 来自法语 joindre，源于拉丁语 jungere「套轭、连接」；同一词根还生出 junction、jugular。

items.en: jungere meant to join or yoke animals together, from jugum, a yoke.
items.cn: jungere 意为把牲口套在一起，源自 jugum「轭」。

items.en: junctus was its past participle, giving the stem junct- seen in junction.
items.cn: 过去分词 junctus 给出 junct- 词干，见于 junction。

items.en: Old French joindre softened the consonant and dropped the nasal ending in speech.
items.cn: 古法语 joindre 软化了辅音，口语里还丢了鼻音词尾。

items.en: English borrowed join in the thirteenth century for both uniting and becoming a member.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 join，既指连接也指成为成员。

items.en: Join up and join in fixed the phrasal uses in later centuries.
items.cn: join up 与 join in 在后几个世纪固定为短语动词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin jung- stem; the near-meaning group holds verbs for connecting and taking part.
note.cn: 形近组共用拉丁词干 jung-；近义组收表示连接与参与的词。

entries.definition: A place where two parts are connected.
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，指接合处或关节。

entries.definition: A point where things meet, especially roads.
entries.definitionCN: 同源词，指交汇处，尤指路口。

entries.definition: A craftsman who makes wooden joints.
entries.definitionCN: 由 join 加 -er 构成，指细木工匠。

entries.definition: To link two things together.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「连接」，语气更中性。

entries.definition: To go into a place or group.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「进入」，强调走进去。

entries.definition: To register as a member of a course.
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，指注册入学或入会。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from the Latin yoke to the club table on the square.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「轭」走到广场上的招新长桌。

normal.en: Latin jungere meant to yoke animals together.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jungere 意为把牲口套在一起。

normal.en: The same root gives joint, junction, and juncture.
normal.cn: 同一词根生出 joint、junction、juncture。

normal.en: Join a club takes a direct object with no preposition.
normal.cn: join a club 直接跟宾语，不加介词。

normal.en: Join in is used for activities rather than organizations.
normal.cn: join in 用于活动，而不是组织。

normal.en: Join forces means two sides put their strength together.
normal.cn: join forces 指双方把力量合在一起。

abstract.en: To join is to put two edges so close the seam disappears.
abstract.cn: 加入就是把两条边贴到接缝合拢。

abstract.en: A yoke over two necks is the oldest picture of the word.
abstract.cn: 横在两条脖子上的轭，是这个词最老的画面。

abstract.en: Every member is one more thread tied to the same rope.
abstract.cn: 每个成员都是系在同一根绳上的又一根线。

examples.en: He joined the company as a junior clerk.
examples.cn: 他作为初级职员加入了这家公司。

examples.en: Join the two wires and wrap them with tape.
examples.cn: 把两根线接上，再用胶布缠好。

examples.en: Will you join us for lunch?
examples.cn: 你跟我们一起去吃午饭吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佐因」—— 佐理的人进来，就是加入

root: 拉丁语 jungere「套轭、连接」（源自 jugum「轭」）→ 过去分词 junctus → 古法语 joindre → 英语 join。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: becoming a member, fastening things, taking part, meeting and merging, and sharing in an action.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：成为成员、把东西接起来、参加活动、会合，以及一同参与。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two edges brought together until the seam cannot be seen.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条边被凑到一起，直到看不见接缝。

branches.en: THE CLUB TABLE: a name written on a list of members.
branches.cn: 招新桌这条线：名字写进会员名单。

branches.en: THE PIPE LINE: two ends fitted into one collar.
branches.cn: 管子这条线：两个端头套进同一个箍。

branches.en: THE GAME LINE: stepping in while others already play.
branches.cn: 游戏这条线：别人已经在玩时走进去。

branches.en: THE CROSSROADS: two paths becoming one below the bridge.
branches.cn: 路口这条线：两条路在桥下合成一条。

branches.en: THE CHORUS: one voice added to many.
branches.cn: 合唱这条线：一个声音加进许多声音。

intro.en: Join carries the Latin stem jung- and takes English endings for its family.
intro.cn: join 带着拉丁词干 jung-，其词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives all descend from jungere, to yoke.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词都源自 jungere「套轭」。

items.meaning: to connect or become a member
items.example: They join the parts by hand.
items.exampleCN: 他们手工把零件接起来。

definition_zh: 笑话；玩笑；笑料；开玩笑道；开玩笑的对象
definition_en: something said or done to make people laugh, or a person or thing that invites teasing
core_image: 一桌人听到一句话后同时笑出声，杯子都晃了一下
scene: 晚饭后客厅里坐满亲戚，舅舅讲起年轻时的糗事。His story about the broken chair got the biggest joke of the evening.
sceneCN: 这里 joke 是「笑话」（第 1 个义项：引人发笑的话或事），句意为他把那把坏椅子的糗事讲得成了当晚最大的笑料。画面里的物件：客厅、沙发、茶杯。

pos.zh: 名词：笑话；玩笑；笑料；笑柄
动词：开玩笑；说笑话

derivatives.zh: 由 joke 加 -er 构成，义为「爱开玩笑的人；扑克里的大王」
由 joke 加 -ing 构成，义为「开玩笑的」
由 joking 加 -ly 构成，义为「开玩笑地」
由 joke 加 -y 构成，义为「爱打趣的；轻松逗趣的」

senses.title: Something said to make people laugh
senses.definition: a short story or remark with a funny turn that makes people laugh
senses.definitionCN: 带有出人意料的滑稽转折，使人发笑的话或短故事
senses.example: He told a joke about two penguins on a bus.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲了个关于两只企鹅坐公交的笑话。
senses.why: The core sense is a spoken turn that produces laughter.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一个说出后引来笑声的转折。

senses.title: A playful act or trick
senses.definition: a playful act, often at somebody else's expense
senses.definitionCN: 一种戏耍的举动，常以别人为对象
senses.example: Hiding his shoes was meant as a joke.
senses.exampleCN: 把他的鞋藏起来原本是开玩笑。
senses.why: The word widens from a spoken thing to a done thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从说出来的东西扩大到做出来的东西。

senses.title: A mocking remark
senses.definition: a remark made lightly to tease or mock someone
senses.definitionCN: 轻描淡写地用来取笑或挖苦某人的话
senses.example: The boys made jokes about his new haircut.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩们拿他的新发型说笑。
senses.why: Laughter can be turned on a person, and the same noun follows.
senses.whyCN: 笑声可以转向某个人，同一个名词也跟着转。

senses.title: A person or thing that invites teasing
senses.definition: a person, plan, or object that seems ridiculous to others
senses.definitionCN: 被别人看作可笑的人、计划或东西
senses.example: The new rule became the joke of the whole office.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定成了整个办公室的笑柄。
senses.why: When the funny thing is the target itself, the noun becomes a label for it.
senses.whyCN: 当可笑的对象本身就是目标时，这个名词就变成给它的标签。

senses.title: To speak or act playfully
senses.definition: to say or do something in play, expecting no serious answer
senses.definitionCN: 带着玩闹意味说话或行事，不指望当真回应
senses.example: I was only joking about the price.
senses.exampleCN: 我不过是拿价格开玩笑。
senses.why: The verb keeps the light, half-serious tone of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了名词那半真半假、轻松的语气。

senses.title: Hard to take seriously
senses.definition: used to say that something is so easy or small it is not worth calling a task
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示某事太容易、太微小，不值得称作难题
senses.example: Fixing that is no joke for a beginner.
senses.exampleCN: 对新手来说，修好那东西可不是说说而已。
senses.why: The idiomatic use keeps the word for things that look light but turn heavy.
senses.whyCN: 这个习语义保留了对「看着轻、其实重」的事物使用该词。

intro.en: Joke came from Latin jocus, a jest, through Italian and French before it reached English.
intro.cn: joke 源于拉丁语 jocus「玩笑」，经由意大利语和法语才进入英语。

items.en: jocus meant a jest, a joke, or a playful word.
items.cn: jocus 意为玩笑、笑话或打趣的话。

items.en: Italian gioco carried the sense of play or sport.
items.cn: 意大利语 gioco 带着「游戏、玩」的意思。

items.en: French jocque named a light saying, and English met the word there.
items.cn: 法语 jocque 指轻松的话，英语是在这里遇到这个词的。

items.en: Joke entered English in the seventeenth century as a noun.
items.cn: joke 在十七世纪作为名词进入英语。

items.en: The verb and the phrase no joke followed within a century.
items.cn: 动词用法与 no joke 的说法在一个世纪内跟上。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the joke family; the near-meaning group holds other kinds of fun and laughter.
note.cn: 形近组共用 joke 这一族词；近义组收其他表示玩笑与好笑事物的词。

entries.definition: Someone who jokes, or the highest card in a pack.
entries.definitionCN: 由 joke 加 -er 构成，指爱开玩笑的人或扑克大王。

entries.definition: In a joking manner.
entries.definitionCN: 由 joke 派生，义为「开玩笑地」。

entries.definition: Formal word for playful and humorous.
entries.definitionCN: 同源于拉丁 jocus，较正式的「诙谐的」。

entries.definition: A joke, often in older writing.
entries.definitionCN: 较文雅的说法，义为「玩笑」，多见于旧文字。

entries.definition: A practical joke played on someone.
entries.definitionCN: 指针对某人的恶作剧。

entries.definition: A short joke, often written for a performer.
entries.definitionCN: 口语里指短小的笑话段子。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the Latin jest to the phrase no joke.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「玩笑」走到 no joke 这种说法。

normal.en: Latin jocus is also the source of jocose.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jocus 也是 jocose 的来源。

normal.en: Tell a joke is the standard verb pair.
normal.cn: tell a joke 是最标准的动词搭配。

normal.en: Play a joke on someone means the target is a person.
normal.cn: play a joke on someone 指被开玩笑的是人。

normal.en: A practical joke is done rather than told.
normal.cn: practical joke 是做出来的，不是讲出来的。

normal.en: No joke means something is serious after all.
normal.cn: no joke 表示某事其实很严重。

abstract.en: A joke is a small trap set for laughter.
abstract.cn: 笑话是给笑声设的小陷阱。

abstract.en: The same word can be the laughter and the one laughed at.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既可以是笑声，也可以是被笑的人。

abstract.en: A joke dies the moment it is explained.
abstract.cn: 笑话一解释就死了。

examples.en: She told a joke that made everyone laugh.
examples.cn: 她讲了个让大家发笑的笑话。

examples.en: They joked about the endless rain all week.
examples.cn: 他们整周都拿下不完的雨开玩笑。

examples.en: Nobody could take his excuse as a joke.
examples.cn: 没人能把他的借口当成玩笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「揍客」—— 玩笑开过头，客人就想揍人

root: 拉丁语 jocus「玩笑、戏谑」→ 意大利语 gioco → 法语 jocque → 英语 joke；同族还有 jocose、jocular。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: a funny story, a playful act, a mocking remark, the laughing stock, the verb, and the ironic phrase no joke.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：笑话、玩笑举动、取笑的话、笑柄、开玩笑的动词义，以及 no joke 这一反讽说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spoken turn that ends in a room full of laughter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话的转折让满屋子人笑出声。

branches.en: THE DINNER TABLE: a story with a funny ending.
branches.cn: 餐桌这条线：有滑稽结尾的故事。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN SHOES: a trick done rather than told.
branches.cn: 藏起的鞋这条线：做出来而不是讲出来的玩笑。

branches.en: THE SCHOOLYARD: laughter aimed at a person.
branches.cn: 校园这条线：笑声对准了某个人。

branches.en: THE NOTICE BOARD: a rule that everyone ridicules.
branches.cn: 公告板这条线：被所有人嘲笑的规定。

branches.en: THE HALF-SERIOUS VOICE: the joking verb and the phrase about weight.
branches.cn: 半真半假的口气：开玩笑的动词义与表示分量的说法。

intro.en: Joke takes only English endings; the Latin joc- stem shows up in its formal cousins.
intro.cn: joke 只加英语词尾，拉丁 joc- 词干出现在它较正式的亲属词里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives descend from jocus, a jest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词源自 jocus「玩笑」。

items.exampleCN: no joke 意为非同小可。

definition_zh: 旅程；行程；历程
definition_en: an act of travelling from one place to another, especially a long one, or a long process of change
core_image: 一条从地平线开头、一直延伸到看不见尽头的路
scene: 清早的车站，人提着行李站在站台尽头，列车的灯从远处亮起来。The journey takes nine hours if the trains run on time.
sceneCN: 这里 journey 是「旅程」（第 1 个义项：从此地到彼地的行程），句意为如果列车准点，这趟要九个钟头。画面里的物件：行李、站台、列车灯。

pos.zh: 名词：旅程；行程；历程

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -er 构成，义为「旅行者」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「旅行」
同源于 jour「日」的形近词，义为「日记；期刊」

senses.title: Travel from one place to another
senses.definition: an act of travelling, especially over a long distance
senses.definitionCN: 一次旅行，尤指长距离的
senses.example: The journey across the mountains took three days.
senses.exampleCN: 翻山那一趟走了三天。
senses.why: The basic sense is simply travel between two named places.
senses.whyCN: 最基本的义项就是两个地名之间的一趟走动。

senses.title: The distance travelled
senses.definition: the length of time or distance covered by travelling
senses.definitionCN: 旅行所花的时间或所走的路程
senses.example: It is a two-hour journey by bus.
senses.exampleCN: 坐公交要两个钟头的路程。
senses.why: The same word names the length of the trip, not only the trip itself.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也指这趟路的长度，而不只是这趟出行。

senses.title: A process of change
senses.definition: a long personal or collective process of growth or change
senses.definitionCN: 个人或集体长期成长与改变的历程
senses.example: Learning the language was a journey of small victories.
senses.exampleCN: 学这门语言是一段由许多小胜利组成的历程。
senses.why: Modern English extended the road image to any long process of change.
senses.whyCN: 现代英语把「路」的意象扩展到任何长期的改变过程。

intro.en: Journey began as French journée, "a day", because travel was measured in days.
intro.cn: journey 起初是法语 journée「一天」，因为旅程是按天来算的。

items.en: diurnus meant "of the day", from dies, "day".
items.cn: diurnus 意为「一天的」，来自 dies「日」。

items.en: journee meant "a day's work or a day's travel".
items.cn: journee 意为「一天的活儿或一天的行程」。

items.en: English took it as journee, still meaning a day's travel.
items.cn: 英语借作 journee，仍指一天的行程。

items.en: The meaning widened from one day to any trip.
items.cn: 词义从「一天」扩到「任何一趟行程」。

items.en: Modern usage adds the inner sense of a process of change.
items.cn: 现代用法又添了「内在历程」这一层。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the journ- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for travelling.
note.cn: 形近组共用 journ- 词干；近义组收表示旅行的词。

entries.definition: A daily record or a magazine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「日记；期刊」，同词干。

entries.definition: A skilled worker paid by the day.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「熟练工」，原文为按日计酬。

entries.definition: A person who writes for the news.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「记者」，同词干。

entries.definition: A short journey for pleasure or business.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「一趟」，多指短程。

entries.definition: A long journey by sea or space.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「航行」，多指海上或太空。

entries.definition: A journey visiting several places.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「游览」，多点巡回。

normalIntro.en: These hooks measure the word in days, as the French did.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子像法国人那样，用「天」来量这个词。

normal.en: jour means day in French.
normal.cn: jour 在法语里是「白天」。

normal.en: A journey was once just a day of travel.
normal.cn: journey 原本只是一天的行程。

normal.en: Longer trips needed more jours, so the meaning grew.
normal.cn: 更长的路要更多「日」，词义就扩大了。

normal.en: A journal is what you write at the end of the day.
normal.cn: journal 是一天结束时写下的东西。

normal.en: Learning is a journey without a station.
normal.cn: 学习是一趟没有站台的旅程。

abstract.en: A journey is a straight line bent by weather.
abstract.cn: 旅程是一条被天气弄弯的直线。

abstract.en: The road is measured in days, the change in years.
abstract.cn: 路用天来量，改变用年来量。

abstract.en: Some journeys end where the traveller begins.
abstract.cn: 有些旅程的终点，正是出发时的自己。

examples.en: The journey from the coast to the capital takes a whole day.
examples.cn: 从海边到首都这一趟要一整天。

examples.en: She kept a notebook of every journey she took.
examples.cn: 她每一趟出行都记在一个本子上。

examples.en: His journey from factory worker to teacher took ten years.
examples.cn: 他从工人到教师的这条路走了十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: jour（日）+ ney —— 一段按日子数的路

root: 拉丁语 dies「日」→ diurnus「一日的」→ 古法语 journee「一天的行程」→ 中古英语 journee → 现代英语 journey。同族有 journal、journeyman、journalist。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: travelling somewhere, the distance covered, and a long inner process.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：出门远行、所走的路程，以及长期的成长历程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road starting at the horizon and going out of sight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从地平线起、伸到看不见尽头的路。

branches.en: THE PLATFORM: bags waiting for the departure.
branches.cn: 站台这条线：等着出发的行李。

branches.en: THE MILEAGE: the hours and miles the trip costs.
branches.cn: 里程这条线：这一趟花掉的时间与里数。

branches.en: THE CHANGE: an inner road from one self to another.
branches.cn: 改变这条线：从旧的自己走到新的自己。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: both senses count the trip in time.
branches.cn: 时钟这条线：两个义项都用时间来数一趟路。

branches.en: THE PATIENCE: distance and growth both take days.
branches.cn: 耐心这条线：路程与成长都要一天一天来。

intro.en: Journey is borrowed from French with its day-root jour- intact.
intro.cn: journey 从法语整词借来，含「日」的词根 jour- 完好保留。

latinIntro.en: Latin dies and diurnus stand behind the French word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dies 与 diurnus 藏在法语词背后。

items.example: The root also appears in journal.

items.exampleCN: 它标出「一整天」这段长度。
英语把 journee 改成 journey。
同一个月「日」的词根，写了下来。

definition_zh: 快乐；喜悦；乐事
definition_en: a strong feeling of happiness, or a person or thing that causes it
core_image: 一个人听见好消息，脸上的光一下子亮起来
scene: 门口传来钥匙转动的声音，孩子跑过去，扑进刚下班的父母怀里。Her face lit with joy when the letter arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 joy 是「喜悦」（第 1 个义项：强烈的快乐情绪），句意为信到时她脸上立刻亮起喜悦。画面里的物件：门口、信件、灯光。

pos.zh: 名词：快乐；喜悦；乐事

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ful 构成，义为「快乐的」
由本词加 -ous 构成，义为「充满喜悦的」
加前缀 en- 构成，义为「享受」
由本词加 -less 构成，义为「毫无乐趣的」

senses.title: A strong happy feeling
senses.definition: a deep feeling of delight and gladness
senses.definitionCN: 深切的喜悦与高兴
senses.example: The children shouted with joy when the snow began.
senses.exampleCN: 雪一下起来，孩子们就欢呼起来。
senses.why: The first sense is the feeling itself, with no object attached.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项是情绪本身，不牵扯具体对象。

senses.title: A source of happiness
senses.definition: a person or thing that brings great pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 带来极大快乐的人或事物
senses.example: That old cat is the joy of her life.
senses.exampleCN: 那只老猫是她生活里的欢乐。
senses.why: English often turns a feeling word into the thing that causes it.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把表示感受的词转成引起感受的那个东西。

senses.title: Success in informal speech
senses.definition: a sense of achievement, mostly in the phrase "no joy"
senses.definitionCN: 取得成效的感觉，多见于 no joy 这一说法
senses.example: We tried twice and got no joy, so we called again.
senses.exampleCN: 我们试了两次都没成功，只好又打电话。
senses.why: In informal speech the word also measures whether an attempt worked.
senses.whyCN: 在口语里，这个词还用来衡量一次尝试有没有成。

intro.en: Joy comes from Old French joie, from Latin gaudium, "gladness", from the verb gaudere, "to rejoice".
intro.cn: joy 来自古法语 joie，源自拉丁语 gaudium「喜乐」，后者来自动词 gaudere「欢乐」。

items.en: gaudere meant "to be glad, to rejoice".
items.cn: gaudere 意为「高兴、欢欣」。

items.en: The noun gaudium meant "gladness".
items.cn: 名词 gaudium 意为「喜乐」。

items.en: French softened it to joie.
items.cn: 法语把它软化成 joie。

items.en: English took joie as joy and kept the feeling sense.
items.cn: 英语借作 joy，保留了情感义。

items.en: Idioms like "jump for joy" fixed the word in everyday speech.
items.cn: jump for joy 一类成语把它固定在日常语里。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the j- opening and the feeling family; the near-meaning group holds words for happiness.
note.cn: 形近组共用 j- 开头与同一情感家族；近义组收表示快乐的词。

entries.definition: To get pleasure from something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「享受」，同词根。

entries.definition: Full of joy.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「快乐的」，同族词。

entries.definition: Cheerful in a lively way.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「快活的」，拼写相近。

entries.definition: Great pleasure, often sudden.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「欣喜」，常指突然的。

entries.definition: A quiet state of being pleased.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「高兴」，偏安静。

entries.definition: The general state of being happy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「幸福」，最宽泛。

normalIntro.en: These hooks trace the word back through French to a Latin verb for rejoicing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它经法语追到拉丁语里那个「欢欣」的动词。

normal.en: gaudere is Latin for to be glad.
normal.cn: gaudere 是拉丁语「高兴」。

normal.en: gaudium became joie in French.
normal.cn: gaudium 在法语里成了 joie。

normal.en: joie crossed the Channel as joy.
normal.cn: joie 跨过海峡变成 joy。

normal.en: en- plus joy makes enjoy.
normal.cn: en- 加 joy 就是 enjoy。

normal.en: Add -ful and the feeling fills the word.
normal.cn: 加 -ful，这个词就装满了这种感觉。

abstract.en: Joy is a door opened by surprise.
abstract.cn: 喜悦是一扇被意外推开的门。

abstract.en: The brightest minutes leave the smallest receipts.
abstract.cn: 最亮的那些分钟，留下最小的票据。

abstract.en: A joy shared is simply a joy doubled.
abstract.cn: 分享的快乐，就是把快乐翻一倍。

examples.en: She could not hide her joy at the news.
examples.cn: 听到这个消息，她掩不住喜悦。

examples.en: The garden has been a joy since spring.
examples.cn: 从春天起，这个花园就一直让人愉快。

examples.en: I called the office twice but had no joy.
examples.cn: 我给办公室打了两次电话，都没办成。

dict_mnemonic.text: joie（法语「快乐」）——脸上的那道光

root: 拉丁语 gaudere「欢欣」→ gaudium「喜乐」→ 古法语 joie → 中古英语 joy。同族有 enjoy、joyful、joyous、joyless。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a strong happy feeling, a source of happiness, and the informal sense of success.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：强烈的快乐情绪、带来快乐的人或事，以及口语中的「顺利」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face lighting up at good news.
core.cn: 核心意象：听到好消息时一下亮起来的脸。

branches.en: THE LIGHT: the feeling itself, sudden and warm.
branches.cn: 光这条线：那种突然而温暖的情绪本身。

branches.en: THE CAT: a small thing that keeps giving pleasure.
branches.cn: 猫这条线：源源不断带来快乐的小东西。

branches.en: THE CALL: no joy means the attempt failed.
branches.cn: 电话这条线：no joy 就是没办成。

branches.en: THE GIFT: feelings and their causes share one word.
branches.cn: 礼物这条线：情绪与引起它的事物共用一词。

branches.en: THE OUTCOME: what turns out well becomes a joy.
branches.cn: 结果这条线：办成的事也成了乐事。

intro.en: Joy is a short, old French stem; the endings are where the learning happens.
intro.cn: joy 是个短小的古法语词干，可学的是它后面加的各种词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin gaudere and gaudium are both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gaudere 与 gaudium 均有记载。

items.example: The root hides behind the French form.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根藏在法语形式后面。

items.example: It forms enjoy, to put joy into.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 enjoy，把快乐放进去。

items.example: The verb is the family base.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一族的基座。

items.example: The noun became joie in French.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词在法语里变成 joie。
